subject: Security ask: Helix private deployment — permitlist, proxy behavior & audit trail
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@helixtx.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixtx.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix private deployment - permitlist and outbound expectations

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is gating the private deployment and needs a concise list of: 1) exact egress IPs and ranges we must allow, 2) firewall/port expectations, and 3) how Redwood proves outbound traffic originated from our tenant (audit / evidence).

We attached our internal ask and a simple network diagram (helix_safelist_request_v1.pdf). High level questions from our side:
- Will traffic originate from a stable set of source IPs per-account or from ephemeral pool?
- Do you require inbound firewall openings to any Helix-managed endpoints (we prefer no inbound holes)?
- Does Redwood support TLS SNI-only inspection or do you require a proxy with mTLS to your control plane?

We need to present this to compliance on Friday. Can you confirm a recommended permitlist and an ops checklist?

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Security Ops Lead
Helix Therapeutics
Attachment: helix_safelist_request_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@helixtx.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixtx.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix private deployment - permitlist and outbound expectations

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. I pulled together an initial operational note and a small set of items we need from your network team to finalize the permitlist. See the short answers up front, then an attached snippet we use for firewall rules.

Short answers:
- Source IPs: For Redwood Private (VPC/private-runtime) we can offer either (A) per-tenant static egress IPs (reserved NAT pool) or (B) shared ephemeral pool that we can map via per-tenant NAT translation events. For compliance we recommend option A — we can reserve a stable /29 per customer in our dedicated deployment offering.
- Ports/FQDNs: Outbound allowed TCP 443 to a tight list of FQDNs used for control plane, telemetry ingestion, and model artifact fetches. We do not require any inbound ports to your network for normal operation.
- Proof of origination: We provide an evidence bundle with flow logs, NAT translation table, and a signed audit manifest (per-request) showing timestamped egress records tied to your tenant id.

What we need from Helix to finalize the exact CIDR:
1) Decide whether you want per-tenant static egress IPs (preferred) or ephemeral pool.
2) Confirm whether your egress path uses an outbound proxy (squid/forward proxy) or direct Internet NAT. If you use proxy, tell us if you can present client certs or only SNI/TLS metadata.
3) Provide any internal IP ranges we should avoid when we present ACLs to your firewall team.

I've attached a terse firewall snippet we typically hand to customers (network_snippet_rules.txt) and a draft checklist — Jordan, can you add the exact CIDR ranges for both static and ephemeral options and confirm whether we recommend NAT hairpin behavior? Irene — please append the minimum audit manifest schema. David — note any runtime constraints (ephemeral vs pinned).

I'll compile and return a single permitlist doc in 24 hours.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: network_snippet_rules.txt (text/plain)

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@helixtx.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixtx.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix private deployment - permitlist and outbound expectations

Folks — internal tech notes (for the compiled reply):

Proposal matrix:
- Option A (Recommended): Per-tenant static /29 NAT pool (4 usable IPs). Advantages: simple allowlist, easy audit (one-to-one mapping). Disadvantages: IP exhaustion if many tenants; requires allocation and routing in our tenant overlay.
- Option B: Shared ephemeral NAT pool with per-tenant SNAT mapping events (we log translation table). Advantages: lower IP footprint. Disadvantages: more complex logs to correlate at Helix side.

Firewall snippet (paste-ready):
# Allowlist for Helix private runtime (Option A - static NAT)
# Source: 203.0.113.88/29 (example reserved range)
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.88/29 any -> controlplane.redwood.ai 443
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.88/29 any -> artifacts.storage.redwood.ai 443
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.88/29 any -> telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai 443
# Optional: DNS to 198.51.100.10 (Helix prefer to route DNS internally)
ALLOW UDP 203.0.113.88/29 any -> 198.51.100.10 53

Proxy and inspection notes:
- We support TLS SNI-only inspection for telemetry (SNI allowlist). We do not terminate customer TLS for model payloads.
- If Helix requires mutual TLS from client side, we can run an mTLS front for control-plane interactions (requires cert exchange and setup time).

Evidence and audit manifest fields (Irene, please check):
- tenant_id, nat_source_ip, nat_translated_ip, dst_fqdn, dst_ip, dst_port, timestamp_utc, request_id, signed_by_redwood (signature blob).

Ops constraints:
- If you choose static IPs, provisioning lead time is 2–3 business days once we have PO and IP assignment.
- If Helix uses an outbound proxy that rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, we will need client-side certs or a stable proxy identity.

I'll mark the example CIDR above as placeholder. Neha, if that aligns, we can draft a final PDF for Samira with a mutual action plan (PO / IP assignment / smoke test).

—Jordan
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@helixtx.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixtx.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix private deployment - permitlist and outbound expectations (final)

Hi Samira / Ben — attaching the finalized permitlist and an ops checklist for your firewall team + a short runbook for the smoke test. Key points summarized below and next steps.

Attachments: private_deploy_diagram.png, network_snippet_rules.txt, helix_safelist_request_v1.pdf (we included an answer sheet)

Summary / next steps:
1) Decision: Please confirm Option A (static per-tenant NAT) or Option B (shared ephemeral). We recommend A for compliance posture.
2) If Option A: provide the PO and accept the proposed /29 allocation. We will schedule provisioning (2 business days) and share the final IPs.
3) If you have an outbound proxy that terminates TLS: send the proxy configuration and whether it preserves SNI and client certs. If not, we expect direct outbound NAT and SNI-based allowlisting is sufficient.
4) Smoke test: after IPs are assigned, allow TCP 443 to controlplane.redwood.ai and telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai, then run a 15-minute tokenized traffic test (we provide test harness).

Evidence package: after the smoke test we will provide a signed audit manifest (JSON) and flow log extract covering the test period + NAT translation table slice. Sample fields: tenant_id, sample_request_id, nat_source_ip, nat_translated_ip, dst_fqdn, dst_port, timestamp_utc, redwood_signature. Irene confirmed schema is good.

If you want us to convert the snippet into a vendor-ready PDF for your firewall change board, say the word and we'll generate it and include the exact /29 values.

Thanks — aiming to get this into your compliance review today.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
